english.title: Burglary dwelling and theft - no violence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having entered as a trespasser

(A)_[a dwelling,]_
(B)_[part of a dwelling,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..),

(C)_[stole therein **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..) to the value of **(..SPECIFY THE VALUE..)]_
(D)_[stole therein **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..) of a value unknown]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 9(1)(b) of the Theft Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
entered as a trespasser
a dwelling / part of a dwelling stole therein

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also H1646 for burglary dwelling where violence is used or threatened - which makes that offence triable ONLY on indictment.
(ii) IMPORTANT - Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Two prior convictions for domestic burglary may make him/her liable to a minimum sentence of three years imprisonment under the provisions of section 314 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment.

See Note (iii) above re increase in penalty

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
